notes: Source: Canon's official "EOS C400 Technical Specifications" PDF (regional Canon Australia/NZ reseller-hosted copy of the manufacturer datasheet), page 7 "Input/Output Terminals" table — this is the authoritative Canon spec sheet, cross-checked against Canon Europe/Canon CNA regional spec pages and B&H listing via search snippets. SDI OUT is rated 12G/6G/3G/HD-SDI (graded as sdi-12g, its max); MON. is rated 3G/HD-SDI (graded sdi-3g). Ethernet is stated elsewhere as 1000BASE-T compatible (eth-1g); the Canon spec PDF itself only says "Yes" without stating speed. TC, G-LOCK, SYNC, and RET terminals are physically small DIN 1.0/2.3 coaxial connectors (not full-size BNC or standard multi-pin DIN) — mapped to "bnc" as the closest connector id in the allowed list since none of hdmi/sdi/bnc/etc. options include a miniature coax DIN connector; treat these four as approximate. REMOTE A is a 2.5mm sub-mini stereo jack, mapped to trs-3.5 (closest available connector; actual size is 2.5mm not 3.5mm). LENS terminal (RF mount + 12-pin lens contacts) and the Multi-function accessory shoe (21-pin, with power contacts) are proprietary lens/accessory mount interfaces, not general AV signal/power ports, and were omitted. Battery power (BP-A30N/BP-A60N, mounted battery plate) is separate from the DC-IN 12V 4-pin XLR barrel-style external DC input, which is the port listed. No rack-mount form factor — this is a handheld/shoulder cinema camera body (approx. 142 x 135 x 135 mm), so rackUnits is omitted.
